entries.def:
βεβαιόω, -ῶ 
(βέβαιος), [in LXX: Ps 40 (41)12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119)28 (קוּם pi.), 3Ma.5.42 * ;] 
to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Rom.15.8 of persons (DCG, ii, 605): 1Co.1.8, 2Co.1.21. Pass., 1Co.1.6, Col.2.7, Heb.2.3; 13.9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; see next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).†
(AS)

βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ 
(βεβαιόω, which see), [in LXX: Lev.25.23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wis.6.19 * ;] 
confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Php.1.7 εἰς β., Heb.6.16, a phrase frequently in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104ff.; Cremer, 140).†
(AS)

βέβηλος, -ον 
(βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל ;] 
__1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence, 
__2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1Ti.4.7; 6.20, 2Ti.2.16; of men, 1Ti.1.9, Heb.12.16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).
† (AS)

βεβηλόω, -ῶ 
(βέβηλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלל ;] 
to profane: τ. σάββατον, Mat.12.5 τ. ἱερόν, Act.24.6 (Cremer, 141).† 
SYN.: κοινόω, which see (AS)

Βεελζεβούλ (WH, App., 159, Rec., βεελζεβούλ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord, and the Talmudic זִבּוּל, from זֶבֶל, dung (Dalman, Gr., 137.n), or perh. זִבֻל, habitation, but, see DB, iv, 409f.; DCG, i, 181). The AV, RV, Beelzebub, comes through Vg. from 2Ki.1.2, בַּעַל זִבוּב, lord of flies (LXX, βάαλ μυῖα, Sm., βεελζεβούβ), 
Beelzebul, Beelzebub, a name of Satan: Mat.10.25; 12.24, 27 Mrk.3.22, Luk.11.15, 18, 19.†…

Βελίαλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּלִיַּעַל, worthlessness, but see DB, i, 268), 
Belial, a name of Satan: 2Co.6.15, Rec. See next word.†
Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl. (another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac pronunciation," or else Heb. בֵּל יַעַר, lord of the forest), 
Beliar, a name of Satan: 2Co.6.15 (see DB, i, 269).†
(AS)

βέλος, -εος, τό 
(βάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵץ ;] 
a missile, a dart: Eph.6.16.† 
(AS)

βελτίων, -ον (genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, 
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] 
neut. as adv., better, very well: 2Ti.1.18 (also Act.10.28 D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.†
(AS)

Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין), 
Benjamin: Act.13.21, Rom.11.1, Php.3.5, Rev.7.8.†
(AS)

Βερνίκη (elsewhere Βερενίκη), Macedonian form of Φερενίκη, cf. Veronica, Victoria), -ης, ἡ, 
Bernice, Berenice, dau. of Herod Agrippa I: Act.25.13, 23; 26.3o.†
(AS)
